title: Homotopy pullback invariance under coherent weak-equivalence cubes
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, simplicial homotopies, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For maps of Kan complexes $u:U\to W$, $v:V\to W$, put
$$P(u,v)=U\times_{W,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,W}V.$$
A homotopy-commuting square consists of maps $f:A\to U$, $g:A\to V$, $u:U\to W$, $v:V\to W$ and a specified homotopy $H:uf\simeq vg$. Its comparison is $A\to P(u,v)$, $a\mapsto(f(a),g(a),H(a,-))$; the square is a homotopy pullback when this is a weak homotopy equivalence. This includes a strictly commuting square by taking the constant homotopy.
Consider two such squares and weak homotopy equivalences $a:A\to A'$, $b:U\to U'$, $c:V\to V'$, $d:W\to W'$. Suppose the four side faces commute up to specified homotopies, and these homotopies together with $H,H'$ form a coherent cube: the two composite boundary paths from $duf$ to $v'g'a$ are homotopic relative endpoints, with one composite passing through $dH$ and the other through $H'a$. Then the comparison of $P(u,v)$ with $P(u',v')$, obtained by applying $b,c,d$ and the two side-face homotopies of the spans, is an isomorphism in the homotopy category of Kan complexes. Here path concatenations mean their homotopy classes, represented by simplicial maps after Kan fillers are chosen; no canonical strict concatenation is asserted. The cube coherence identifies the two maps from $A$ to $P(u',v')$ up to homotopy. Consequently one square is a homotopy pullback if and only if the other is. The assertion is stable under a zigzag of such comparisons.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.9, evaluation-equivalence argument, supplies the context; the coherent-cube path-pullback lemma is the explicit agent argument extracted from the retained item proof, old step 1, not a verbatim assertion of 02X4. Archival Kerodon copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $I=\Delta^1$ and $T=\operatorname{Fun}(I,W')$. By [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan], $T$ is Kan. Each evaluation $e_i:T\to W'$ is a trivial fibration: a lifting problem against $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ transposes to extension into $W'$ from $(I\times\partial\Delta^n)\cup(\{i\}\times\Delta^n)$ to $I\times\Delta^n$. This inclusion is the pushout-product of a boundary monomorphism with the endpoint horn $\{i\}\hookrightarrow I$, hence anodyne by [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]. The Kan condition fills it, and the boundary-lifting characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] applies, including $n=0$. All path pullbacks below are Kan by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison]. Name the span-face homotopies $\alpha:du\simeq u'b$ and $\beta:dv\simeq v'c$, viewed as maps $U\to T$ and $V\to T$. Name the other faces $F:bf\simeq f'a$ and $G:cg\simeq g'a$. Oppositely oriented specified faces can be represented in these orientations by filling the outer two-horns in the appropriate Kan mapping space; no reversal map of $I$ is used.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.3 and the endpoint restriction case; explicit pushout-product lifting. The orientation adjustment is the outer-horn inverse construction in a Kan complex.

proof.text: Form $R=P(\alpha,\beta)=U\times_{T,e_0}\operatorname{Fun}(I,T)\times_{e_1,T}V$. Here the evaluations in this formula are in the new path parameter $s$; write $t$ for the path parameter inside $T$. Evaluation at $t=i$ gives $r_i:R\to P_i$, where $P_0=P(du,dv)$ and $P_1=P(u'b,v'c)$. These are strict span maps with vertex maps $\mathrm{id}_U,\mathrm{id}_V,e_i$. Step 1 and [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] make both $r_i$ weak equivalences. The same node gives weak equivalences $j:P(u,v)\to P_0$ induced by $(\mathrm{id}_U,\mathrm{id}_V,d)$, and $k:P_1\to P(u',v')$ induced by $(b,c,\mathrm{id}_{W'})$. Its strict-commutation hypotheses hold by the definitions of $du,dv,u'b,v'c$; it is not applied directly to a homotopy-commuting face.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.9, applied to the four explicitly strictly commuting span maps.

proof.text: The map $r_0$ has the right lifting property against every boundary inclusion. Indeed a boundary lifting problem prescribes a map to $W'$ on $(I_s\times\partial\Delta^n\times I_t)\cup(\partial I_s\times\Delta^n\times I_t)\cup(I_s\times\Delta^n\times\{0\})$: these three parts are respectively the given boundary in $R$, the prescribed paths $\alpha,\beta$, and the given simplex of $P_0$. They agree on intersections. Put $B=I_s\times\Delta^n$ and $B_0=(I_s\times\partial\Delta^n)\cup(\partial I_s\times\Delta^n)$. The inclusion of the prescribed union into $B\times I_t$ is $ (B_0\hookrightarrow B)\mathbin{\square}(\{0\}\hookrightarrow I_t)$, anodyne by [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]. Fill into the Kan complex $W'$. Thus $r_0$ is a trivial fibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. As every monomorphism is built from boundary inclusions, $r_0$ lifts against every monomorphism. Lifting $\varnothing\hookrightarrow P_0$ gives a section $\sigma$. Any two sections are homotopic over $P_0$ by lifting $P_0\times\partial I\hookrightarrow P_0\times I$, with base the projection to $P_0$.

source.place: Explicit relative-square extension, a single pushout-product lifting argument; boundary-lifting and monomorphism generation from the existing Kan-Quillen core node.

proof.text: Define $\Psi=k r_1\sigma j:P(u,v)\to P(u',v')$. Since $r_0\sigma=1$, two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] and Step 2 make $\sigma$, hence $\Psi$, weak equivalences. They therefore become isomorphisms in the homotopy category. Its endpoint coordinates are $b,c$. Its path coordinate $\eta$ is the $t=1$ edge of the square supplied by $\sigma$, whose $t=0$ edge is $d\gamma$ and whose $s=0,1$ edges are $\alpha,\beta$. Triangulating this square and applying [lem-coef-edge-homotopy-quotient-calculus] gives $[\alpha][\eta]=[d\gamma][\beta]$, with products here and below written in traversal order. Outer two-horn fillers give inverses to every edge class in a Kan complex, so $[\eta]=[\alpha]^{-1}[d\gamma][\beta]$. This is exactly the prescribed span comparison. The section homotopy of Step 3 shows independence of its filler choices. Equivalently its class is the roof $[k][r_1][r_0]^{-1}[j]$, without choosing a strict concatenation operation.

source.place: Edge.CompStruct.nonempty_iff, lines 295-297, for the two triangles; model two-out-of-three and the explicit roof of Step 2.

proof.text: Let $q:A\to P(u,v)$ and $q':A'\to P(u',v')$ be the given comparison maps, and let $\lambda:A\times I\to W'$ be the path coordinate of $\Psi q$. Work in the Kan complex $M=\operatorname{Fun}(A,W')$, which is Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan]. Step 4 gives $[\alpha f][\lambda]=[dH][\beta g]$. The cube hypothesis gives $[dH][\beta g][v'G]=[\alpha f][u'F][H'a]$. To interpret its relative-endpoint homotopies in the edge quotient, triangulate a relative homotopy square: its two constant endpoint edges are identities, so the triangle composition rule of [lem-coef-edge-homotopy-quotient-calculus] equates the two path classes. Thus cancellation of the invertible class $[\alpha f]$ gives $[\lambda][v'G]=[u'F][H'a]$ in $H_L(M)$. The equality uses the specified cube coherence, rather than only the classes of its vertices or its four vertical equivalences.

source.place: HomotopicL, quotient category, and triangle composition criterion, lines 78-79 and 203-311; direct application to the supplied relative-endpoint cube coherence.

proof.text: Choose a triangle in $M$ composing $\lambda$ and $v'G$, and denote its diagonal by $z$. Such a triangle exists by the Kan condition. By Step 5, the composite of $u'F$ and $H'a$ has the same class $[z]$. The if-and-only-if in [lem-coef-edge-homotopy-quotient-calculus] supplies a triangle with exactly those two edges and the same diagonal $z$. Glue the two triangles along $z$ to obtain a simplicial square in $M$ with bottom $\lambda$, top $H'a$, and side edges $u'F,v'G$. By the internal-functor definition this is a map $A\times I\times I\to W'$. Together with $F:A\times I\to U'$ and $G:A\times I\to V'$ it defines a homotopy $A\times I\to P(u',v')$ from $\Psi q$ to $q'a$: the two path endpoints agree with $u'F,v'G$ at every simplex. Hence the cube coherence gives precisely the asserted homotopy of comparison maps.

source.place: Edge.CompStruct.nonempty_iff, lines 295-297, supplies the second triangle with its prescribed diagonal; the square gluing and internal-functor adjunction are elementary.

proof.text: Homotopic maps have the same weak-equivalence status: for each Kan target $Z$, postcomposing a homotopy with a map into $Z$ makes the two precomposition operations equal on edge components of internal functor spaces. Thus the testing criterion of [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence] gives the claim. Apply it to the homotopy in Step 6. Since $\Psi$ and $a$ are weak equivalences, two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] gives: $q$ is a weak equivalence if and only if $\Psi q$ is, if and only if $q'a$ is, if and only if $q'$ is. This is the desired equivalence of homotopy-pullback properties under the definition in the statement.

source.place: Corollary 3.6.4.3, Kan-target testing criterion; elementary precomposition with the constructed homotopy and model two-out-of-three.

proof.text: For a finite zigzag, apply Steps 4 and 6 to each comparison. Its maps are isomorphisms in the homotopy category, invertible in either direction, and the homotopies identify the successive comparison maps there. Composing these isomorphisms gives the comparison along the zigzag. Repeated application of Step 7 preserves and reflects the homotopy-pullback property along every edge, hence between the two ends. The length-zero zigzag is the identity.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.9 is the invariance context; this last step is composition of the already proved isomorphisms.

lean.statement: theorem kan_homotopy_coherent_cube_invariance (s s' : KanCubeSquare.{u}) (cube : KanCoherentCube s s') : ∃ comparison : CoherentPathModelComparison cube.b cube.c cube.d cube.H_u cube.H_v, IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence comparison.map ∧ (∃ (h : KanComplex (simplicialHomotopyPullback s.u s.v)) (h' : KanComplex (simplicialHomotopyPullback s'.u s'.v)), IsIso (spaceWeakEquivalences.Q.map (ObjectProperty.homMk (X := ⟨simplicialHomotopyPullback s.u s.v, h⟩) (Y := ⟨simplicialHomotopyPullback s'.u s'.v, h'⟩) comparison.map))) ∧ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (s.comparison ≫ comparison.map) (cube.a ≫ s'.comparison)) ∧ (∀ comparison' : CoherentPathModelComparison cube.b cube.c cube.d cube.H_u cube.H_v, Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy comparison.map comparison'.map)) ∧ (s.IsHomotopyPullback ↔ s'.IsHomotopyPullback)
lean.note: The square apex is an arbitrary simplicial set; only U,V,W are required Kan.
